newsitem.title: NORWAY: Storebrand head unfamiliar with major buyer.
newsitem.headline: Storebrand head unfamiliar with major buyer.

text.p: The chief executive officer of Storebrand ASA, Norway's biggest insurer, said on Wednesday he did not know who had been buying large amounts of shares in the company recently.
"I know just as little as you do," Age Korsvold said in response to a question at a news conference where he presented Storebrand's 1996 results.
Oslo Bourse said in a statement that media company Schibsted ASA had booked a profit of 12.3 million crowns on Tuesday on the sale of 322,000 ordinary shares in Storebrand.
"The shares were sold on behalf of several subsidiaries," the short statement said.
Market players last week reported there was a huge demand for Storebrand shares.
Tabloid Verdens Gang said on Wednesday that Norwegian entrepreneur and investor Kjell Inge Roekke, top shareholder in industrial group Aker RGI ASA, was the secret buyer of Storebrand stock.
"So far Roekke and his partners are said to have secured about 10 percent of Storebrand," the newspaper said.
It said controlling Storebrand, which has a fat stock portfolio, would be part of Roekke's corporate takeover strategy in Norway.
"By acquiring control of Storebrand, Aker RGI would be able to buy controlling stakes in other Norwegian companies much cheaper," Verdens Gang said.
Roekke was not available for a comment, but an Aker RGI spokesman told Reuters: "Aker RGI has not bought any shares in Storbrand."
